 K-pop ticket sales in Singapore rise nearly 19-fold since 2022, says Ticketmaster
 SPINS 
 1.6K 
 Estimated:   reading 
 Words by Hidzir Junaini 
 First published: 18 November 2026 
 Last updated: 18 November 2026 
 News 
 Gigs 
 Events 
 Tech & Business 
 K-pop acts are playing bigger venues and adding more concert dates in Singapore, with new figures from Ticketmaster showing a sharp increase in ticket sales.
 In an announcement on 18 November , the ticketing company revealed that K-pop ticket sales in Singapore for 2026 to date have reached almost 19 times their 2022 level. The number of K-pop events listed on Ticketmaster Singapore has also grown more than eightfold over the same period.
 According to Ticketmaster’s data, more than half of K-pop shows in Singapore since 2022 were nearly sold out. Between 2022 and 2026, nine acts expanded their Singapore performances by moving to larger venues, adding dates, or both.
 SEVENTEEN , MAMAMOO , ITZY , IVE , Stray Kids , i-dle , and BABYMONSTER moved to bigger venues, while BLACKPINK , ENHYPEN , and BABYMONSTER added show dates on subsequent visits.
 “Singapore loves K-pop, and that love keeps growing. What stands out in our data is the breadth of demand,” said Shawn Quek , managing director of Ticketmaster Singapore and Taiwan.
 “Beyond the headline acts, fans are turning out for a wide range of artists, from stadium concerts to intimate fan events. That creates more opportunities for artists to connect with audiences here and across the region.”
 The audience also extends beyond Singapore. Between 2022 and 2026, fans based outside the country accounted for more than 25% of annual K-pop ticket sales on average, according to the company.
 Guo Teyi , director of the Leisure Events Division at the Singapore Tourism Board , highlighted the role these concerts play in attracting visitors.
 “K-pop is a powerful draw for visitors to Singapore, with fans across the region making the trip not just for the concert, but to experience everything our city has to offer,” she said.
 “We look forward to welcoming even more visitors to Singapore through the shared passion for live music.”
